# Design of this implementation

Stack-specific guidance for this implementation of the app: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*The following is Angular's official best-practices rules file, included verbatim from
<https://angular.dev/assets/context/best-practices.md>. It is part of the Angular
architecture.*

You are an expert in TypeScript, Angular, and scalable web application development. You write functional, maintainable, performant, and accessible code following Angular and TypeScript best practices.

## TypeScript Best Practices

- Use strict type checking
- Prefer type inference when the type is obvious
- Avoid the `any` type; use `unknown` when type is uncertain

## Angular Best Practices

- Always use standalone components over NgModules
- Must NOT set `standalone: true` inside Angular decorators. It's the default in Angular v20+.
- Do NOT set `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` explicitly. `OnPush` is the default in Angular v22+.
- Use signals for state management
- Implement lazy loading for feature routes
- Do NOT use the `@HostBinding` and `@HostListener` decorators. Put host bindings inside the `host` object of the `@Component` or `@Directive` decorator instead
- Use `NgOptimizedImage` for all static images.
  - `NgOptimizedImage` does not work for inline base64 images.

## Accessibility Requirements

- It MUST pass all AXE checks.
- It MUST follow all WCAG AA minimums, including focus management, color contrast, and ARIA attributes.

### Components

- Keep components small and focused on a single responsibility
- Use `input()` and `output()` functions instead of decorators
- Use `model()` for two-way bound properties with `[(prop)]` syntax instead of pairing `input()` with `output()`
- Use `computed()` for derived state
- Use `linkedSignal()` for state derived from multiple reactive sources that must stay synchronized
- Prefer inline templates for small components
- Prefer Signal Forms (`@angular/forms/signals`) for new forms. They are stable in Angular v22+ and provide signal-based state, type-safe field access, and schema-based validation
- When not using Signal Forms, prefer Reactive forms instead of Template-driven ones
- Do NOT use `ngClass`, use `class` bindings instead
- Do NOT use `ngStyle`, use `style` bindings instead
- Do NOT import `CommonModule`, import only the directives and pipes the template uses, such as `AsyncPipe` or `DatePipe`
- When using external templates/styles, use paths relative to the component TS file.

## State Management

- Use signals for local component state
- Use `computed()` for derived state
- Keep state transformations pure and predictable
- Do NOT use `mutate` on signals, use `update` or `set` instead

## Templates

- Keep templates simple and avoid complex logic
- Use native control flow (`@if`, `@for`, `@switch`) instead of `*ngIf`, `*ngFor`, `*ngSwitch`
- Use the async pipe to handle observables
- Do not assume globals like (`new Date()`) are available.

## Services

- Design services around a single responsibility
- Use the `providedIn: 'root'` option for singleton services
- Prefer the `@Service` decorator over `@Injectable({providedIn: 'root'})` for new singleton services (Angular v22+)
- Use the `inject()` function instead of constructor injection

---

## Spring

This is a standard Spring Boot application, built with conventional Spring MVC
(`@RestController` request handling, a service layer, Spring Data / JPA persistence, and Bean
Validation). Follow ordinary Spring conventions and idioms throughout. Spring's reference
documentation is the guidance for the server: Spring Boot
<https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/4.1/reference/> and Spring Framework
<https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/reference/>.

import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { resetAndSeed } from '../support/seed';
import { auditLines } from '../support/audit';

// Generate copies a recurring invoice's period lines as adjusted by its adjustment notes: a change
// of quantity carries into the next period, a line taken off by a credit note is not copied, and a
// line added by a debit note with a service period is copied like the invoice's own. An invoice
// that was generated from another (invoices[].recurringFrom) is that one's next period, so the
// earlier invoice can't generate again; the plan still ends at its end date
// (invoices[].recurUntil).
test.describe('generating from an adjusted invoice', () => {
  test('generating from an adjusted invoice copies its lines as adjusted', { tag: '@core' }, async ({ page }) => {
    await resetAndSeed({
      asOf: '2026-06-10',
      settings: { taxRate: 10 },
      clients: [{ id: 1, name: 'Acme Ltd', email: 'ops@acme.example' }],
      invoices: [
        { id: 9, clientId: 1, status: 'SENT', issueDate: '2026-05-01', dueDate: '2026-05-31', recurring: true,
          lineItems: [
            { id: 1, description: 'Support plan', qty: 1, unitPrice: 450, periodStart: '2026-05-01', periodEnd: '2026-05-31' },
          ] },
        { id: 10, clientId: 1, status: 'SENT', issueDate: '2026-06-01', dueDate: '2026-06-30',
          recurring: true, recurringFrom: 9, recurUntil: '2026-12-31',
          lineItems: [
            { id: 2, description: 'Support plan', qty: 1, unitPrice: 450, periodStart: '2026-06-01', periodEnd: '2026-06-30' },
            { id: 3, description: 'Licences', qty: 10, unitPrice: 60, periodStart: '2026-06-01', periodEnd: '2026-06-30' },
            { id: 4, description: 'Setup', qty: 1, unitPrice: 120 },
          ] },
      ],
    });
    await page.goto('/');

    await page.getByTestId('client-row-1').click();
    // invoice 9 already generated June's invoice 10
    await page.getByTestId('invoice-row-9').click();
    await page.getByTestId('invoice-generate').click();
    await expect(page.getByTestId('invoice-generate-error')).toBeVisible();
    await page.getByTestId('invoice-row-10').click();
    await expect(page.getByTestId('invoice-panel-number')).toHaveText(await page.getByTestId('invoice-row-10').getByTestId('invoice-number').innerText());
    await page.getByTestId('line-row-3').getByTestId('line-edit').click();
    await page.getByTestId('line-form-qty').fill('12');
    await page.getByTestId('line-form-submit').click();
    // two more licences for June: 120.00 a month for 30 days, 120 x 12 / 365 x 30 = 118.36, plus tax
    await expect.poll(() => auditLines()).toContain('ADJUSTMENT_ISSUED id=11 number=ADJ-0000117 invoice=10 total=130.20');
    await page.getByTestId('line-row-2').getByTestId('line-remove').click();
    await expect.poll(() => auditLines()).toContain('ADJUSTMENT_ISSUED id=12 number=ADJ-0000125 invoice=10 total=-488.22');
    await page.getByTestId('invoice-generate').click();
    // July: 12 licences and no support plan, as adjusted; the one-off setup is not copied.
    // 720 x 12 / 365 x 31 = 733.81, plus tax; sent at once
    await expect.poll(() => auditLines()).toContain('INVOICE_GENERATED from=INV-0000109 to=INV-0000133');
    await expect.poll(() => auditLines()).toContain('INVOICE_SENT id=13 number=INV-0000133 total=807.19');
    await page.getByTestId('invoice-row-13').click();
    await expect(page.getByTestId('invoice-panel-number')).toHaveText(await page.getByTestId('invoice-row-13').getByTestId('invoice-number').innerText());
    await expect(page.getByTestId(/^line-row-\d+$/)).toHaveCount(1);
    await expect(page.getByTestId('line-row-7').getByTestId('line-qty')).toHaveText('12');
    await expect(page.getByTestId('line-row-7').getByTestId('line-period')).toHaveText('2026-07-01 to 2026-07-31');
  });
});

content.text:
Generate now builds the next period from the invoice's lines as its adjustment notes left them. `bin/e2e` passes: the acceptance test and the replay of earlier fixtures.

**How it works now**
- **Quantity changed on a note:** the difference is added to or taken off the original line, so 10 licences raised to 12 are copied as 12.
- **Line taken off on a credit note:** its quantity is subtracted from the line it credits. A line left with nothing to bill isn't copied, which is how the removed support plan drops out.
- **New line on a debit note:** copied like the invoice's own lines if it has a service period, and skipped if it doesn't, the same as before.
- **Other edits:** a change to anything other than quantity is already made as "credit the old line, bill the new one". So the next period gets the new version of the line.

Only notes that have been issued count; drafts and void notes are ignored.

**What changed**
- `Invoice.java`: `nextPeriod` takes the invoice's issued notes and copies from a new helper, `periodLinesAsAdjusted`, instead of the raw lines.
- `InvoiceService.generateNext`: looks up those notes and passes them in.

No database, seed or front-end changes were needed.

**Untested case:** the next period's dates are still worked out from the invoice's own lines. If a debit note added a line whose service period ends later than every line on the invoice, the next period would not move to follow it. That matches "everything else stays the same", but the test doesn't cover it.
